findings.title: A rate does not apply on its own effective date
findings.trigger: Posting dated on the day a new EUR rate takes effect, for example 2026-02-01 with rates dated 2026-01-01 and 2026-02-01.
findings.impact: bisect_left finds the matching date's own slot, so minus one selects the previous rate: the entry is booked at January's rate, and a posting on the first rate's date raises MissingRate. Every posting on a rate change day carries the wrong USD amount. Use bisect_right.

findings.title: Revaluation silently skips balances that have no closing rate
findings.trigger: Close January while a EUR account holds a balance and treasury has not loaded a EUR rate dated 2026-01-31.
findings.impact: closing() returns None and the loop continues, so the account is not revalued, close_period still locks the period, and the books close at a stale USD value with no error. A missing closing rate has to stop the close (closing_rate raises MissingRate).

findings.title: Migrated import keys use a different format from the importer
findings.trigger: Run migration 0003 on existing books, then re-import a statement that was already imported, which the importer promises is safe.
findings.impact: The migration writes 'TX-1@operating' while import_key() builds 'operating:TX-1', so no migrated key matches and every previously imported line is posted a second time, doubling bank balances. The migration should write import_key(source, reference).
